articles.title: 'Dinheiro esquecido': BC diz que R$ 5,8 bilhões podem ser resgatados; quase 24 milhões de pessoas têm direito | G1
articles.standfirst: Em maio, o governo Lula anunciou o uso de parte dos recursos não retirados por clientes das instituições financeiras para viabilizar o Desenrola 2.0. TCU apura manobra; entenda.
articles.summary: Em maio, o governo Lula anunciou o uso de parte dos recursos não retirados por clientes das instituições financeiras para viabilizar o Desenrola 2.0. TCU apura manobra; entenda.
articles.body:
O Banco Central (BC) atualizou os dados e informou nesta terça-feira (13) que ainda existem, nas instituições financeiras, R$ 5,79 bilhões em "recursos esquecidos" pelos clientes.

O balanço considera valores contabilizados até agosto deste ano.

R$ 4,31 bilhões são recursos de 23,94 milhões de pessoas físicas;

R$ 1,48 bilhão são valores de 2,36 milhões de empresas.

O sistema do BC permite consultar se pessoas físicas (inclusive falecidas) e empresas deixaram valores para trás em bancos, consórcios ou outras instituições.

Governo anunciou uso do dinheiro; TCU apura

No começo de maio, o governo anunciou o uso, de R$ 5 bilhões a R$ 8 bilhões , dos recursos esquecidos pelos trabalhadores nos bancos para viabilizar descontos no Desenrola 2.0 – novo programa de renegociação de dívidas.

No fim de maio, parte do dinheiro, cerca de R$ 5,7 bilhões, foi encaminhada para um fundo público, o Fundo de Garantia de Operações (FGO), para oferecer garantias às instituições financeiras, ou seja, parte do dinheiro desse fundo vai cobrir eventual calote dos tomadores de crédito.

"Os recursos não reclamados serão utilizados para o FGO garantir operações do próprio sistema financeiro. Haverá segregação de 10% do saldo transferido que ficará disponível para cobrir eventuais pedidos de resgate [pelos correntistas]", informou o governo à época.

Como informou o g1 em junho, o caso entrou na mira do Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) . Técnicos do tribunal apuram o uso de recursos para programas federais por fora do orçamento público.

Por não passar pelo orçamento da União, os recursos não estão dentro dos limites de gastos que têm de ser obedecido. Pelas regras, os gastos não podem crescer mais de 2,5% ao ano (acima da inflação).

Se fosse incluído formalmente no orçamento, e consequentemente no limite de gastos, o governo teria de bloquear igual montante em outras despesas livres (discricionárias), aumentando as dificuldades em um ano eleitoral .

Relatório do Banco Central dos EUA de 2022 afirmou que o PIX é uma moeda digital — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

O único site no qual é possível fazer a consulta e saber como solicitar a devolução dos valores para pessoas jurídicas ou físicas, incluindo falecidas, é o .

🔑Via sistema do Banco Central, os valores só serão liberados para aqueles que fornecerem uma chave PIX para a devolução.

📞Caso não tenha uma chave cadastrada, é preciso entrar em contato com a instituição para combinar a forma de recebimento. Outra opção é criar uma chave e retornar ao sistema para fazer a solicitação.

💰No caso de valores a receber de pessoas falecidas, é preciso ser herdeiro, testamentário, inventariante ou representante legal para consultá-los. Também é necessário preencher um termo de responsabilidade.

Após a consulta, é preciso entrar em contato com as instituições nas quais há valores a receber e verificar os procedimentos.

articles.title: Elon Musk explains why chip stocks are getting drilled on news out of China
articles.body:
Hot chip stocks like Micron ( MU ) and Sandisk ( SNDK ) are taking it on the chin out of the gate this week.

Ask the world's richest person, Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, and he will probably say the sell-off is just beginning.

"When China figures out how to manufacture a product, their ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined. We saw this with lithium batteries and solar, for example," Musk said in a new post on X .

Musk was replying to a post about the fresh chip stock sell-off, which is being fueled by Chinese tech player CXMT . The company's president, Cao Kanyu, called out "key progress" on a new cell architecture at an event in Shanghai over the weekend.

CXMT plans to roll out new memory products based on the architecture by the end of the year.

The development sparked concern that growing Chinese competition could threaten memory chip pricing power, causing investors to unwind crowded momentum AI trades.

Micron shed 3.8% in Monday's trading session and is down another 4% in premarket trading today. Sandisk lost 5.9% on Monday and is off by 5% today.

Sharp sell-offs are also being seen in other memory names, including SK Hynix ( SKHY ), Western Digital ( WDC ), and Seagate ( STX ).

Added Musk, "SpaceX is a rare counter-example, where its mass to orbit is roughly an order of magnitude greater than the rest of the world, BUT China now does the majority of non-SpaceX mass to orbit. SpaceX is an anomaly in the matrix. Maybe RAM will be different, but RAM was a low margin commodity only ~3 years ago. LP5 and LP6 are designed to a common standard that China seems to be solving fast."

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the ' Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team. articles.title: IBM India’s Patel sees ‘digital swaraj’ shaping India’s AI opportunity
articles.summary: IBM India MD Sandip Patel says “digital swaraj” and sovereign AI will shape India’s opportunity, backed by IBM Sovereign Core and Bharat Core AI stack.
articles.body: Mumbai: IBM India and South Asia managing director Sandip Patel said his call for “digital swaraj” reflects businesses’ and govts’ growing need to exercise greater control over their data, technology assets and the systems that manage them.“I have started calling this the era of digital swaraj. In a predominantly digital world and a global digital economy, organisations need a degree of digital sovereignty suited to their level of regulation and the criticality of their operations,” Patel told TOI.Geopolitical developments and regulatory requirements have heightened concerns over data sovereignty, particularly among organisations in regulated sectors such as banking. Companies increasingly want clarity on where their data resides, who controls encryption keys, where the control plane is located, and whether compliance can be demonstrated continuously.IBM’s Sovereign Core, announced in March, is designed to address these concerns. The software stack can be deployed in a client- or partner-owned data centre, providing cloud-like capabilities while keeping control-plane operations and key management within the customer’s jurisdiction.Built on Sovereign Core, IBM Bharat Core is an AI stack optimised for India, offering reusable Indic AI services, models and connectors across industries. It is benchmarked for quality and scale in Indian scenarios and guides users through the AI lifecycle by recommending suitable building blocks and infrastructure tailored to India’s requirements. IBM is also developing India-specific tools to accelerate Sovereign Core implementation, while its Svaiam reference architecture is designed to help deploy sovereign AI capabilities within govt environments.The shift towards greater control over technology infrastructure is also supporting India’s data centre growth. Patel identified two drivers: companies building capacity in India to support global operations, and Indian enterprises investing in infrastructure they can control themselves. For IBM, the opportunity spans hardware, sovereign infrastructure software and tools to monitor assets and improve data centre efficiency.IBM is also applying AI internally to improve productivity. Patel said the company initially targeted $2 billion in savings over three years but achieved $4.5 billion in operational savings by the end of last year through automation, simplification, process redesign and AI. Its AI coding agent, Bob, is being used by about 80,000 engineers, with productivity gains of 45%, including among client teams, he said.IBM’s business has shifted towards higher-value software, hardware and consulting following the 2021 spin-off of its infrastructure services business, Kyndryl. IBM India’s consolidated revenue from operations rose 7.7% year-on-year to Rs 32,804 crore in FY25, compared with Rs 30,459 crore in FY24, according to MCA data sourced from data intelligence platform Tofler. Net profit increased 41.8% to Rs 3,968 crore in FY25 from Rs 2,798 crore in the previous financial year.Commenting on the US suspension of PERM processing, a step towards employment-based permanent residency, Patel said IBM was not among the companies named in the announcements and that he did not have details of its filings.“If the US becomes more restrictive on permanent residency, I think that could be good for India. It gives India an opportunity to strengthen its talent base,” he said, adding that PERM and H-1B visas should not be conflated.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Stock market rally today: Sensex ends over 1,100 points up, investors richer by Rs 4.12 lakh crore - what's driving the rise?
articles.summary: Stock market rally today: Indian equity benchmark indices, BSE Sensex and Nifty50, rallied strongly in trade on Tuesday, rising more than 1% in afternoon
articles.body: Stock market rally today: Indian equity benchmark indices, BSE Sensex and Nifty50, rallied strongly in trade on Tuesday, rising more than 1% in afternoon trade. Comments by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax and securities transaction tax, along with a rally in IT stocks and other factors, lifted investor sentiment.BSE Sensex ended the day at 73,033.78, up 1,109 points or 1.54%. Nifty50 closed at 22,721.95, up 359 points or 1.60%.The rally added more than Rs 4.12 lakh crore to the combined market capitalisation of listed companies, taking the total to Rs 470 lakh crore.IT companies led the gains among Sensex constituents. HCL Tech shares climbed more than 5% following the company's second-quarter results, while TCS, another heavyweight in the sector, advanced around 5%. Tech Mahindra and Infosys also rose by approximately 3% each.Why did stock market rally today?LTCG, STT in focusFM Nirmala Sitharaman said on Tuesday that discussions have been underway in domestic and international forums on long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax and securities transaction tax (STT). Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, she noted that both Indian and international investors had been sharing their views on LTCG tax. She added that the debate over transaction tax and whether different asset classes should be taxed in a similar manner had been discussed extensively. Though she refrained from committing to any changes.“We are very close to the budget and the preparation for the budget has started, and it may not be the best time for me to say what I will or what I will not consider,” she said.Her remarks come as India's equity market continues to face substantial outflows amid several challenges. In its Ecowrap report on Monday, SBI Research said the government should consider scrapping LTCG tax on equities, arguing that the move could encourage investors to hold their investments for longer.IT stocks rallyHeavyweight IT stocks surged, helping lift the broader market despite the prevailing headwinds. The decline in global AI-linked stocks has also improved sentiment towards India's prominent technology companies, which have increasingly been viewed as an ‘anti-AI’ trade.South Korea's Kospi, considered a key reflection of the artificial intelligence investment boom, plunged more than 6%, while Japan's Nikkei fell over 2%. Major technology stocks, including Samsung, also suffered steep losses as concerns grew over excessive optimism surrounding the emerging technology. Analysts have warned that the AI rally could be developing into a bubble.ALSO READ: ‘Biggest red flag’: BJP targets Rahul Gandhi over CEC row, alleges track record of briberyRupee posts sharp gainsThe rupee strengthened by 82 paise to 94.96 against the US dollar in early trade on Tuesday, extending its recovery following measures announced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to support the weakening currency.On Monday, the RBI tightened regulations governing rupee non-deliverable derivative contracts, restricting overseas clients to using these instruments only for hedging. It also extended a 20% cash reserve requirement to banks' own rupee currency hedges.These steps followed four measures announced by the central bank on Saturday. They included a dedicated dollar supply window for three state-run oil companies, tighter curbs on foreign exchange derivatives, a 20% cash reserve requirement for certain currency contracts and stricter daily cash reserve requirements for banks.“These steps are expected to reduce pressure on the spot market and curb speculative dollar buying, supporting the currency in the near term. However, sustained recovery will depend on FII flows, crude oil prices and broader dollar movement,” said Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst of Commodity and Currency at LKP Securities.Bond yields ease from multi-year highsAfter climbing to multi-year peaks, bond yields edged lower, providing some relief to equity markets. The yield on the US 10-year Treasury slipped below 5.2%, while the 30-year Treasury yield declined to 5.56%.The yield on two-year US Treasury bonds, which tends to track expectations around Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, also eased below 4.8%.Rising bond yields have recently weighed on stock markets because higher returns from debt instruments can make them more attractive to investors, diverting funds away from equities, particularly in emerging markets. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions, meaning a sharp rise in yields indicates a selloff in the bond market.ALSO READ: Will Budget bring LTCG, STT relief? Here’s what FM Nirmala Sitharaman saidOil prices declineCrude oil prices fell on Tuesday as investors weighed the possibility of additional Russian oil supplies reaching global markets. US President Donald Trump defended his administration's decision to temporarily relax restrictions on Russian diesel supplies.Brent crude futures dropped more than 1%, trading near $105 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures also declined by over 1% to below $93 per barrel.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Broadcom CEO: Investors are ignoring a key lesson from Warren Buffett
articles.summary: In very frank comments, Broadcom CEO Hock Tan called out investors for not knowing what they were investing in, evoking a classic Warren Buffett tenet. But i...
articles.body:
Warren Buffett famously advocated for investing in companies that you understand.

"What an investor needs is the ability to correctly evaluate selected businesses," he wrote in his 1996 letter to Berkshire Hathaway investors . "You only have to be able to evaluate companies within your circle of competence. The size of that circle is not very important; knowing its boundaries, however, is vital."

Broadcom ( AVGO ) CEO Hock Tan says too many people have blown past those boundaries and are blindly investing.

"A lot of investors have no clue what they are investing in," he said in Singapore, Bloomberg reported . These investors, he added, have "extreme expectations only to find out that it's almost like they are in a casino."

Buffett himself was not always the most savvy tech investor, a fact he lamented when discussing Google , which was out of his "circle," so he bought very late. But the rise of even harder-to-understand AI stuff has made following this Buffett tenet way more difficult. We do not all have Ben Affleck-level AI comprehension ( watch this if you haven't ), and no one wants to get left behind.

It's easy to see where Tan and Buffett are coming from, and why the latter advocated for a simple index fund , arguing most people would be better off.

To be clear, Tan is bullish — he runs Broadcom. But in the long term, he's worried about the industry running out of capital and admits that profitability will hinge on proving AI's utility to businesses. Many of which, he said, might be just "wasting money."

Tan's reminder can be said another way: Yes, all the impressive AI things we see are very impressive. But they are also impressive in the same way a Ferrari is impressive — it can drive like that because it's expensive. And that it may not actually be that useful for its high cost in every business case.

Still, it's hard for regular retail investors not to see the massive bets made by Meta ( META ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and others and not assume they're simply following an entity that knows more than they do about the technology and its implications — with conviction strong enough to bet huge on it.

But perhaps the lesson is in the nuance of Tan's comments: Avoid the "casino" aspect of the AI trade, not necessarily the trade itself. With a huge chunk of the S&P 500 bolstered by AI, you can't anyway, even if you heed the Oracle of Omaha's still-relevant advice.

Ethan Wolff-Mann is a Senior Editor at Yahoo Finance, running newsletters. Follow him on X @ewolffmann .

articles.title: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman avoids commitment on LTCG, STT changes ahead of Budget
articles.summary: Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday declined to indicate whether the government would make changes to long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax
articles.body: Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday declined to indicate whether the government would make changes to long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax or securities transaction tax (STT), saying it was too early to comment as preparations for the upcoming Union Budget had begun.Replying to a question at an event, Sitharaman said investors in India and abroad had been discussing the taxation of capital gains and different asset classes and the government was open to hearing their views.“We are very close to the budget and the preparation for the budget has started, and it may not be the best time for me to say what I will or what I will not consider,” she said at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026, as cited by news agency ANI.Her remarks come a day after a report by SBI Research proposed abolishing LTCG tax on equity investments to encourage longer-term investments and help stabilise foreign capital flows.SBI Research proposes scrapping LTCG tax on equitiesSBI Research has called on the government to consider extending the holding period for equity investments to two or three years while abolishing LTCG tax on equities.“The government must seriously look into anchoring hot money flows into equity segment by extending the holding period to say 2-3 years and abolishing the long-term capital gains tax for equity,” the report said.The proposal comes amid sustained foreign portfolio investor (FPI) selling in Indian equities.According to figures cited in the report, foreign investors sold shares worth Rs 44,166 crore in October up to the time of publication, taking their total equity withdrawals in 2026 to Rs 3.04 lakh crore.The current LTCG tax rate for foreign investors on equity investments is 12.5 per cent. The Union Budget 2026 retained this rate for listed shares and equity mutual funds, continuing the framework introduced in 2024.SBI Research also called for simplifying the repatriation of export earnings, suggesting a reasonable timeframe of around six months, and sought greater clarity on withholding tax applicable to external commercial borrowings.Sitharaman says RBI focused on curbing rupee volatilityAt the event, Sitharaman also addressed the rupee's depreciation against the US dollar, saying the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was focused on limiting excessive volatility rather than fixing the currency at a particular level.She acknowledged that the rupee had depreciated significantly over the past 18 months, attributing much of the pressure to external challenges. She said India's economic fundamentals and foreign exchange reserves remained sound.“They are not trying to fix the rupee. They are trying to stop the volatility. And for that, there is a lot of effort from the RBI side. So, these efforts from the RBI... will continue not to...fix the rupee. We would appreciate it if the rupee finds its own (value),” she said, according to news agency PTI.Sitharaman's comments followed a series of measures announced by the RBI to curb pressure on the domestic currency. These included a special window for oil marketing companies to meet dollar demand outside the spot market and tighter rules for foreign exchange derivatives trading.The central bank also introduced a reserve requirement linked to certain dollar purchases.The measures supported the rupee, which rose around 1 per cent on Monday. The currency appreciated to Rs 94.96 against the US dollar in early trade on Tuesday.“I'm sure there are efforts which the RBI would take further to make sure that the rupee doesn't become too volatile,” Sitharaman said, adding that India's economic fundamentals remained sound.She also reiterated the government's commitment to fiscal discipline and macroeconomic stability, while maintaining spending priorities in welfare, education and healthcare.Finance minister highlights investment opportunitiesSitharaman also outlined investment opportunities in infrastructure, semiconductors, renewable energy and emerging technologies.On semiconductor manufacturing, she defended India's approach of developing both advanced chips and those used in everyday applications, including refrigerators, automobiles, industrial machinery and Internet of Things devices.She said the expansion of artificial intelligence and data centres would require substantial electricity generation, reliable power infrastructure and sustainable sources of green energy.Investments in transmission networks and renewable energy would be important to meet these requirements.The finance minister said the National Infrastructure Pipeline had grown to more than USD 4.5 trillion, offering opportunities across sectors and regions.She also highlighted the role of the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development and the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund in mobilising long-term capital.Sitharaman further said domestic private investment was gaining momentum in areas including renewable energy, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals and aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul facilities.She noted that India's civil aviation sector was growing at around 16 per cent, creating additional investment opportunities in aviation-related infrastructure and services.You use AI every day. articles.title: Farmer sold fruits and vegetables at APMC, deposited cash in bank account, but faced notice for unexplained large deposits; ITAT Bangalore gives relief, accepts land records and sale bills as proof
articles.summary: Is your income from agricultural sources taxable?
articles.body: Is your income from agricultural sources taxable? A farmer from Bengaluru who grew vegetables and fruits and sold them to Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC) for cash faced a tax notice for unexplained income.However, he was able to successfully challenge an income tax notice over large cash deposits in his bank account. The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Bangalore, ruled in his favour after he produced evidence to support his explanation for the deposits.What the case is aboutThe man owned just over four acres of agricultural land which he used for growing fruits and vegetables. According to him, the produce was sold for cash at an Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC) yard.The Income Tax Department questioned the farmer’s financial activities after he deposited large sums of cash into his bank account and was also involved in the sale and purchase of a property.The department suspected a mismatch between these transactions and the income disclosed in his income tax return (ITR). This prompted it to issue a notice seeking an explanation for the cash deposits.To substantiate his account, the man furnished copies of his land records, bills which documented the sales at the APMC yard and also bank statements. He maintained that the deposits were money earned from agricultural activities.The man also said he understood that agricultural income was exempt from tax and, therefore, did not need to be disclosed in his ITR.The Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO), however, was not convinced by his explanation. The officer noted that the Record of Rights, Tenancy and Crops (RTC) documents did not specify which crops the man had cultivated, leaving the AO questioning how his land had generated such substantial cash receipts from agricultural sales.The AO also pointed out that the taxpayer had not reported expenditure on seeds or other inputs required to grow the fruits and vegetables. In the officer's assessment, the absence of any declared cultivation-related expenses raised doubts about the man’s claim that he had produced and sold the crops.Another concern was that the man had not disclosed agricultural income in either the preceding years or the subsequent year. Taking these factors into account, the AO rejected his explanation and treated the substantial cash deposits as unexplained cash credit under Section 69.The Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), or CIT(A), subsequently considered the man’s arguments but dismissed his appeal, holding that he had not supported his explanation with credible evidence.He then challenged the decision before ITAT, Bangalore. On August 28, 2026, the tribunal ruled in his favour.Why did the farmer win the case?The ITAT Bangalore observed that the tax authorities' objections centred on two issues: the farmer had not disclosed the agricultural income in his ITR, and the documents submitted did not clearly identify the crops grown on his land.To examine the matter, the tribunal considered the RTC and pahani records relating to the agricultural land owned or cultivated by the man. It also examined the monthly summaries of sale bills and the individual bills for agricultural produce sold through the APMC market.The documents established that Ramachandrababu owned the land in question.The tribunal pointed out that RTC records are maintained by the Karnataka state authorities. The absence of details about the crops in these records did not establish that the man had not grown any agricultural produce.The tribunal further observed that the AO's objections might have carried weight if the officer had conducted additional enquiries to establish whether the man's claims were genuine. However, no such verification had been carried out.On the issue of missing purchase records, the ITAT Bangalore observed that it was not reasonable to expect someone engaged in small-scale agricultural activities to maintain the formal, detailed records that the AO had demanded.After considering the taxpayer's submissions and the documents he had furnished, including the APMC sale bills, the ITAT Bangalore accepted his explanation.The tribunal consequently concluded that the cash deposits were supported by agricultural income and could not be classified as unexplained money under Section 69A.Akhil Chandna, Partner and Global People Solutions Leader at Grant Thornton Bharat, told ET that the landowner was able to establish where the cash deposited in his bank account had come from.He supported his explanation that the money was agricultural income by producing relevant documents, including agricultural land records, APMC sale bills and bank statements.The ITAT Bangalore observed that the Income Tax Department had neither presented evidence contradicting the taxpayer's account nor carried out an independent investigation to verify and disprove his explanation.The tribunal also took into consideration the practical circumstances of small-scale farming. It held that the lack of detailed records of agricultural inputs, shortcomings in land records maintained by the government, or the absence of agricultural income declarations in earlier years could not, on their own, invalidate a claim that was otherwise supported by evidence.Chandna says: "Accordingly, since the landowner could establish a credible nexus between the agricultural activities, cash sale proceeds and subsequent bank deposits, the ITAT Bangalore held that such deposits could not be treated as unexplained money under Section 69A of the Income-tax Act, 1961."You use AI every day. articles.title: TOI Founders’ Forum 2026: Entrepreneurs share stories of grit, growth and innovation
articles.summary: What does it take to build a business that lasts?
articles.body: What does it take to build a business that lasts? That question shaped the conversations at The Times of India’s Founders’ Forum 2026, where entrepreneurs and business leaders came together to share the realities of building enterprises, overcoming setbacks and creating meaningful impact.Sponsored by Garodia International, the event offered valuable perspectives from founders who have turned ideas into thriving businesses.Dr P. Anbalagan, IAS, Principal Secretary, Industries, Investment and Services Department, Government of Maharashtra, attended the event as the chief guest and felicitated the participating entrepreneurs for their contributions to the entrepreneurial ecosystem. Stories of grit and growthThe event featured two engaging panel discussions. The first, titled ‘Building Businesses and Breaking Barriers’, featured Dr. Ajay Yadav, founder and director of Physio Fit Guru (Halcyon Physiotherapy Pvt. Ltd.); Kishor Kumar, founder and chairman of the ICH IIMM National Balgandharva Kala Academy Pariwar and Swarn Bharat Tulsi Foundation; Basharul Islam Munna, founder and CEO of Travel Bazaar Global; and Professor Dr Sanjay B. Chordiya, founder, president and chairman of the Suryadatta Education Foundation (SEF), Pune.The conversation centred on resilience, innovation and the courage to move ahead despite challenges.The discussion also highlighted the importance of a supportive ecosystem, strong values and long-term thinking in building sustainable businesses. Success with purposeThe second panel explored how entrepreneurs can move beyond commercial success to create meaningful and lasting impact. The discussion featured Pawan Kaushik, founder of PNP Polymers Pvt. Ltd.; Abhishek Mhatre, anchor, actor, TEDx speaker and digital content creator; Dr Vikas Kikan, vice president of Centre of Sustainability for Pure Earth and CEO of Beyond Drilling and Exploration Pvt. Ltd.; and R.K. Mitra, founder and CEO of Inditron Enterprises Pvt. Ltd.The event concluded with a strong message: successful businesses are built not only on innovation and perseverance, but also on the ability to create opportunities and inspire future entrepreneurs.Meet the founders and business leadersDr. Ajay Yadav, Founder & Director, Physio Fit Guru (Halcyon Physiotherapy Private LTD):Dr. Ajay Yadav is an accomplished Musculoskeletal & Sports Physiotherapist with over 18 years of clinical experience and the Founder of PhysioFit Guru, a premium Advanced Spine & Sports Rehabilitation Centre in Mumbai1. Recognised for his commitment to advancing modern physiotherapy and rehabilitation, Dr. Yadav has developed PhysioFit Guru into a technology-driven rehabilitation centre integrating advanced spine rehabilitation, sports injury management, robotic spinal decompression, scanning laser therapy, shockwave therapy, pelvic floor rehabilitation and medical gym-based functional recovery.Hemant Jain, Joint Managing Director, Kewal Kiran Clothing Limited (KKCL) - Killer Jeans:Killer emerged in 1989 as one of India's first homegrown denim brands, quickly gaining prominence for its rebellious spirit and innovative designs. What began as a single pair of jeans has evolved into a movement of rebellion, confidence, and unapologetic self-expression. Today, Killer stands as a brand of power. Killer Jeans is one of the largest-selling denim brands in India. While it started with jeans, the brand's portfolio now spans men's ready-to-wear apparel including jeans, trousers, cargos, capris, shirts, jackets, and t-shirts, as well as innerwear (vests and briefs), kids apparel, footwear (shoes and socks), time-wear, eyewear, and other addictive accessories like belts and bracelets.R.K. Mitra, Founder and CEO, Inditron Enterprises Pvt. Ltd:R.K. Mitra has been recognised for his visionary leadership, entrepreneurial excellence, and significant contribution to the water and wastewater treatment industry. His commitment to innovative Water treatment, sewage treatment, effluent treatment and Zero Liquid Discharge solutions has contributed to sustainable water management, resource conservation, and environmental responsibility across diverse industrial sectors and international markets.Jayshree Jindal, Partner - Jindal Cocoa LLP, Founder - Cocoburst:Cocoburst is a premium chocolate brand by Jindal Cocoa built on quality, innovation and great taste. With a portfolio spanning a variety of chocolates, spreads, and customised gifting, it is a contemporary Indian chocolate brand with international standards.Pawan Kaushik, Founder, PNP Polymers Pvt. Ltd.:PNP is a company that believes in hard work, sincerity and loyalty, which have helped it become a leading brand in coated cloth. Its defining trait is its ability to provide a wide range of quality products and services across India, with its own warehouses spread over 20 lakh sq. ft.2 The team at PNP has always focused on delivering quality products with quality after-sales service at the most competitive prices, which has helped it become a market leader. With a sustainable competitive advantage arising from its strong brand, high credibility, market leadership across businesses and large customer base, the company delivers quality products and after-sales service at fair prices, helping markets function better. PNP Group has a diversified portfolio of products ranging from nylon yarn for the textile market to HAO turbo ventilators and tie roofing screws for industrial applications, as well as Synwood products for the interior and exterior beautification of living spaces.Dr. Vikas Kikan, Vice President Centre of Sustainability for Pure Earth, CEO - Beyond Drilling & Exploration Pvt. Ltd.:The man turning burnt fields into a national asset. Every year, millions of tonnes of agricultural residue are burnt across India, creating an environmental challenge. But where many see waste, Kikan saw a resource waiting to be unlocked. He built his business around a powerful conviction that crop residue could be transformed from something we burn into something we can use, value and build upon. articles.title: El Niño, costlier crude may keep inflation elevated: Piramal Finance economist
articles.summary: India's retail inflation in September was largely in line with the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) projections, but adverse weather conditions and elevated
articles.body: India's retail inflation in September was largely in line with the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) projections, but adverse weather conditions and elevated global crude oil prices could prolong pressure on food and fuel prices, Debopam Chaudhuri, Chief Economist at Piramal Finance, said on Tuesday.In an exclusive interview with ANI, Chaudhuri said markets had already anticipated a gradual increase in Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation, with the latest figures showing no significant or unexpected surge in prices.“Looking at inflation in the September quarter, it is exactly at the rate the RBI had forecast. There is no indication of runaway inflation in the data, and I believe the central bank will continue with its existing approach,” he said.However, Chaudhuri cautioned that unfavourable weather patterns and persistently high international crude oil prices could create additional inflationary pressures in the months ahead.El Niño raises concerns over food pricesDiscussing the potential impact of El Niño, Chaudhuri said the weather phenomenon could affect both kharif crop output and the sowing of rabi crops, potentially keeping food inflation elevated for longer than anticipated.“The El Niño we are experiencing this year is turning out to be one of the most severe since the 1980s,” he said.He also pointed to high global crude oil prices as a concern for the Indian economy, noting that they were increasing the country's import bill and adding to imported inflation.On currency movements, Chaudhuri said intervention by the central bank and a possible weakening of the US dollar could offer some short-term relief. However, he warned that the inflationary impact of expensive crude oil could take longer to subside.He added that businesses were likely to gradually transfer higher input costs to consumers, potentially sustaining inflationary pressures across the eLeconomy.Rural consumption may face greater pressureChaudhuri said rising inflation in rural areas could weigh on consumer spending, while urban consumption was likely to expand at a faster pace.He attributed the expected divergence to the differing effects of inflation on rural and urban households.“I am expecting to see urban spending to be much faster than rural spending because of this dichotomy in the way inflation is hitting these two segments,” he said.RBI rate outlook and FY27 growth forecastOn monetary policy, Chaudhuri expects the RBI to maintain its existing interest rates at its December meeting, given that inflation remains broadly consistent with the central bank's projections.“I don't expect another rate hike in December, primarily because the inflation that we have seen so far is pretty much in sync with RBI expectations,” he said.However, he expects the RBI to consider a gradual tightening of monetary policy in the months that follow, with potential increases of 25 basis points each in February and April.Despite the risks from adverse weather and higher import costs, Chaudhuri remained positive about India's growth prospects. He projected the economy to expand by approximately 6.9 per cent in the financial year 2026-27 (FY27).“Overall, I think the growth rate in FY27 should be close to around 6.9 per cent,” he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Nilekani-backed Fundamentum AI fund raises Rs 3,000 cr
articles.summary: Nilekani-backed Fundamentum’s third fund raises Rs 3,000 crore, lifts target to Rs 3,500 crore to back Indian AI and deeptech startups with larger cheques.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Nandan Nilekani-backed Fundamentum’s third fund has secured Rs 3,000 crore from investors and increased its fundraising ceiling to Rs 3,500 crore following strong demand, as the venture capital firm prepares to make larger bets on Indian artificial intelligence and deeptech startups.The fund, managed by Fundamentum Frontier Advisors (F2A), is led by Fundamentum co-founder Ashish Kumar. In an interview with TOI, Kumar said the firm has already closed the Rs 3,000 crore and is negotiating with institutional investors to raise another Rs 500 crore. It expects to complete the final close within the next two months.About 70% of the capital has come from Indian investors, largely family offices, while overseas investors account for the remaining 30%. Nilekani is the fund’s anchor investor and mentor.F2A plans to invest Rs 100-200 crore each in 12-15 companies over the next two to three years. It is already in advanced discussions to close three investments this quarter, with the first announcement expected as early as this month or November.The fund’s larger cheque sizes reflect a decision to take bigger stakes in companies rather than a rise in startup valuations, Kumar said. F2A had earlier indicated investments of Rs 50-150 crore.“We will take more of the round,” he said, adding that the fund also wants to invest more in subsequent rounds as its portfolio companies grow.Kumar believes India’s growth-stage deeptech market remains significantly undervalued compared with more developed markets. “Series B deeptech in India is a mispriced asset,” he said, estimating that comparable companies in Western markets could command valuations three times as high.He attributed the gap partly to a shortage of domestic investors capable of leading large funding rounds. While early-stage deeptech funds have multiplied, few have the capital required to lead Series B investments, he said.According to Kumar, India currently has more than 50 deeptech companies that have reached a stage where they could attract Series B funding. These include around seven robotics companies, seven to nine semiconductor startups and another eight or nine businesses working on data centre infrastructure, including cooling, power and energy systems.He estimates that another eight to 10 companies are reaching this stage every quarter.Unlike conventional software startups, deeptech companies do not necessarily need substantial revenue to qualify for growth-stage funding, Kumar said. Instead, investors look for developed technology, an identifiable commercial use case and at least one reference customer.The fund will invest across consumer AI, enterprise software and deeptech infrastructure, including robotics, semiconductors, quantum technologies and advanced materials.Kumar also pointed to an emerging trend of experienced Indian technology professionals returning from the US to build deeptech businesses in India.Of F2A’s three proposed investments, one involves a company originally established in the US that is shifting its domicile to India. Another involves founders returning after working overseas.“It’s almost the second reverse brain drain happening,” Kumar said, comparing the trend with the return of Indian professionals who helped build the country’s technology and financial services businesses two decades ago.He said access to larger pools of domestic capital could also help Indian founders retain intellectual property and build their companies locally rather than moving overseas for funding.F2A is led by three general partners: Kumar, former SIDBI Venture Capital executive Debraj Banerjee and Vivek Singla. The firm will focus on companies that have validated their technology and are ready to expand commercially, including into overseas markets.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Govt commits Rs 7,131 cr to 19 fund managers under RDI scheme
articles.summary: Government commits Rs 7,131 crore to 19 fund managers under Rs 1 lakh crore RDI scheme to back high-risk R&D in AI, robotics, quantum, space and biotech.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Govt has committed Rs 7,131 crore to the first group of 19 fund managers selected under its Rs 1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) scheme. The group comprises 14 alternative investment funds and five focused research organisations that will channel capital to eligible technology companies.Blume Ventures, Chiratae Ventures, Kalaari Capital, Speciale Invest, YourNest Capital, IvyCap Ventures, Ideaspring Capital and TVS Capital Funds are among the selected managers. The list also includes Sixth Sense Ventures, Celesta India AIF Managers, AdvantEdge Investment Managers, AMA Capital Advisors, Translation Endeavors and Campus.The five research organisations are AI & Robotics Technology Park (ARTPARK) at IISc Bengaluru; Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms (C-CAMP) in Bengaluru; IIT Madras Research Park; Pilani Innovation & Entrepreneurship Development Society at BITS Pilani; and Society for Innovation & Entrepreneurship at IIT Bombay.The Empowered Group of Secretaries approved the first group at its October 8 meeting, according to a govt release dated October 12. The selected managers are expected to raise private capital equivalent to the RDI fund’s contribution. Individual allocations were not disclosed in the published list.The fund is managed by an independent business unit within Anusandhan National Research Foundation, under Department of Science and Technology. Applications for the first group opened in January 2026. Selection involved an assessment of proposals and interactions with an expert advisory committee.Launched in November 2025, the scheme aims to provide long-term capital for research and development involving high risks. Its priority areas include artificial intelligence, robotics, quantum technologies, space, biotechnology, healthcare and energy transition.Govt said it would continue inviting applications and selecting additional groups of fund managers in the near future.You use AI every day. articles.title: Bumble to Go Private in $1.3 Billion Deal With Ithaca Holdings
articles.summary: Dating-app company Bumble Inc. is being taken private by newly formed firm Ithaca Holdings for $1.3 billion.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Dating-app company Bumble Inc. is being taken private by newly formed firm Ithaca Holdings for $1.3 billion.

Ithaca Holdings will pay $6.05 per share, according to a statement on Monday. Bloomberg reported on Monday that Bumble and Ithaca Holdings were in advanced talks about a sale. The deal price represents a 138% premium over Bumble's closing share price on Friday, the last trading day before Bloomberg and other news outlets reported on a possible deal.

After the deal is completed, Bumble will remain based in Austin with other major offices in London and New York.

The deal marks a dramatic turn for Bumble, which was valued at $14 billion when it went public more than five and a half years ago. The app was founded in 2014 by Whitney Wolfe Herd, a former Tinder cofounder, on the premise that only women could make the first move on the app. But Bumble, like many of its dating-app peers, has suffered user declines as young people have grown fatigued with online dating and have shown an interest in other forms of meeting, including in-person events.

In August, Bumble ditched the women-go-first model, its latest move to boost user engagement. The company this year also introduced an artificial intelligence-powered assistant designed to act as a personal matchmaker, offering an alternative experience to swiping through user profiles.

In the statement, Wolfe Herd said she would "remain actively involved with Bumble."

Bumble shares were halted ahead of the announcement. The stock had surged 50% on Monday to close at $3.80, its best single-day gain since the company went public on Feb. 11, 2021.

Ithaca Holdings was founded earlier this year by Sequoia Capital partner Ravi Gupta and former Meta Platforms Inc. Chief Revenue Officer John Hegeman with a plan to acquire at least one public or private firm and infuse it with new technology, potentially including AI, Bloomberg reported in March.

articles.title: RBI’s ‘bazooka’ sees rupee rising 1.4% versus dollar in two days, but should central bank let it fall?
articles.summary: Where is the rupee headed? The Indian currency has been in a free fall for several quarters now.
articles.body: Where is the rupee headed? The Indian currency has been in a free fall for several quarters now. At one time its one-year forward even breached the 100 mark prompting experts and economists to wonder if the rupee will cross the 100 mark versus the US dollar.A lot has changed since then. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has stepped in to build a record foreign exchange reserves chest to arm itself with tools to intervene in the forex market. The FCNR(B) deposits scheme helped attract billions of dollars, putting India in a comfortable position on the forex reserves front.Yet continued capital outflows, high oil prices, uncertainty on the US-Iran war front, and rising US bond yields have added pressure to the currency, pushing it to record lows of almost 97.More recently, RBI’s measures unveiled last week have led to the rupee appreciating sharply. On Friday it closed at 96.61. Since then it has appreciated by Re 1.36 or 1.41% to 95.24.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();One thought process is that the RBI should allow the market forces to let the rupee find its levels. Indeed the IMF recently said that India should allow the exchange rate to act as a shock absorber.Interestingly, RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra believes that the rupee is actually undervalued.A currency is said to be undervalued when it is weaker than what experts believe is its fair value based on underlying economic fundamentals.However, an undervalued currency does not automatically mean it will strengthen soon. The currency can continue to remain weak for an extended period because of capital outflows, global uncertainty or other market pressures.What should RBI do? How effective would its latest measures be for long-term prospects of rupee? And, should the rupee be allowed to depreciate?RBI’s measuresLast week, RBI unveiled what SBI Research has called a bazooka to protect the rupee’s slide.These measures were:RBI opened a direct dollar-supply window for three state-run OMCs shifting roughly $10-12 billion per month away from the open spot market.The daily CRR maintenance has been raised to 99% and simultaneously to tighten liquidity in the system the RBI has announced a Rs 25,000 crore OMO sales.RBI has tightened foreign exchange derivative regulations by prohibiting the rebooking of cancelled rupee derivative contractsIt has lowered the threshold for taking FX derivative positions without underlying exposure from $100 million to $5 million across all Authorised DealersIt has strengthened documentation requirements to prevent duplicate hedging, and introduced a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve for larger contracts.Vivek Kumar, Economist at QuantEco sees RBI’s special measures as a comprehensive package for addressing both internal and external macro pressures.“The dual focus on increasing the price of money (i.e., interest rate) and restricting its availability (i.e., draining surplus liquidity) is an appropriate policy response to the emerging inflation and currency risks,” Vivek Kumar tells TOI.In addition, tighter regulation of rupee hedging and trading will dramatically shrink space for speculation and short-circuit the self-fulfilling expectation of currency weakness.How long will the effect last?The effect may however be short-term.Interest rate increases by the US Federal Reserve have historically put emerging markets under pressure through shifts in capital flows, financing conditions and exchange rates.The Federal Reserve raised rates on September 17, marking its first increase since July 2023.As Vivek Kumar points out: the underlying pressure on the rupee from a firm dollar, elevated energy prices, and continued portfolio outflows persists.“As such, while these measures will help to stabilise the rupee, they won't engineer a reversal beyond the initial knee-jerk relief rally. Since the rupee remains exposed to the current set of adverse global factors, durable stability will be conceivable only if the global tensions ease,” he says.“Meanwhile, the RBI could focus on maintaining an ex-ante real policy rate of 1.0-1.5% to ensure durable macroeconomic balance. This can be complemented with measures to attract foreign investment,” he adds.Yet another important factor is the central bank’s stance that it will not target any particular level of the rupee versus dollar. Any intervention will be aimed at curbing speculative pressures and volatility.Ranen Banerjee of PwC India says that the recent measures taken by RBI will surely address the pressures on rupee caused by speculative trades.“These measures are not towards addressing the fundamentals of demand and supply of forex but more to make the supply more orderly for the oil companies and make the demand for forex real and not speculative,” he explains.SBI Research says that while the RBI has been taking all possible steps to thwart a seemingly difficult global playbook, there is an urgent need also by the government to address some of the long pending structural issues regarding capital inflows. For example, it recommends abolishing the long-term capital gains tax on equities. This would help deal with capital outflows more effectively.Should RBI let the rupee depreciate?There are the costs associated with a weaker rupee.While exports benefit from a depreciating currency, imports become costlier. In the current scenario, with oil prices high, it acts as a double whammy when India imports higher inflation.And, the inflationary pressures for a net importing country like India increase with a weaker rupee. The fiscal pressures also increase owing to higher energy and fertiliser costs in rupee terms.Sujan Hajra, Chief Economist at Anand Rathi Group notes that the immediate costs are especially relevant for India, whose crude-oil import dependence reached approximately 88.7% in FY2025–26, according to PPAC data. “Depreciation compounds an oil-price shock, raising domestic production costs and potentially inflation. It also increases the rupee burden of unhedged foreign-currency debt, reduces purchasing power and can weaken foreign investors’ dollar returns. Crucially, depreciation raises the rupee cost of imports immediately; improvement in the dollar trade balance requires a subsequent response in export and import volumes,” he explains.Hence, experts say the aim should be to have the exchange rate closer to the real effective exchange rate and not target a particular exchange rate.Radhika Rao, Senior Economist and Executive Director at DBS Bank cautions against the fallout of letting rupee depreciate.“While exchange-rate flexibility is a shock absorber, policymakers will be mindful of the risk that one-way currency depreciation can become self-reinforcing. Preventing a disorderly depreciation is therefore as important as preserving flexibility,” she tells TOI.“Beyond a point, it can become destabilsing for capital flows, price stability and sentiments, requiring an active policy response,” she adds.Rao is of the view that the breadth of the restrictions highlight the authorities view that the USD/INR is nearing a defacto red line and that the recent bout of rupee depreciation is being viewed as disorderly rather than fundamentals driven.Ranen Banerjee, Partner and Leader, Economic Advisory at PwC India says that the rupee should find its natural level based on the dollar forex demand and supply.“Targeting an exchange rate is always futile as we have only limited firepower and means to address external factors that determine forex flows. Volatility owing to speculation on the rupee needs to be managed and that is what RBI is doing,” he tells TOI.As Sujan Hajra points out: A record low against the dollar does not, by itself, establish whether the rupee is cheap or expensive. “Valuation requires examining inflation-adjusted exchange rates against trading partners, productivity and the external balance. Equally, a fundamentally undervalued currency can weaken temporarily when dollar demand exceeds supply,” he tells TOI.“I favour calibrated intervention to prevent self-reinforcing depreciation, alongside sufficient flexibility to accommodate persistent external pressures. The objective should be orderly adjustment and anchored inflation expectations,” he says.Economists believe that the economy’s growth momentum, demand in the Indian economy and the opportunities for growth are being currently overshadowed by capital flows to AI centred investments, higher yields in the developed markets and higher oil prices.“It is a cycle and we need to manage the macro through this cycle as there has been no change in the underlying fundamentals of the Indian economy as can be seen from the growth forecasts being upgraded by almost all external agencies,” Banerjee says.IMF may favour market-driven exchange rate adjustments, but for RBI orderly currency movements assume priority.And, as the RBI governor pointed out, the rupee is undervalued, which means the economy’s fundamentals do not warrant such sharp levels of depreciation.DK Srivastava, Chief Policy Advisor at EY India says the US dollar remains overvalued and the rupee undervalued.“Rising US bond yields are attracting capital flows into the US, including from India, adding pressure on the rupee and deepening its undervaluation,” he tells TOI.“In this environment, the RBI should continue to guide the rupee along a trend consistent with inflation differentials. While inflation remains elevated in both economies, India’s CPI inflation averaged 4.8% during June-September 2026, compared with about 3.4% in the US during June-August 2026, suggesting that some depreciation may be warranted,” Srivastava adds.You use AI every day. articles.title: How buying mobile phones on EMI is leading to reduced defaults on two-wheeler loans
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Consumer durable loans, such as buying a mobile phone on EMI, are helping lenders build credit histories for younger borrowers, contributing to a
articles.body: MUMBAI: Consumer durable loans, such as buying a mobile phone on EMI, are helping lenders build credit histories for younger borrowers, contributing to a decline in two-wheeler loan delinquencies to a seven-year low of 1.4% in June 2026 from 2.7% in June 2019, according to TransUnion CIBIL.First-time borrowers accounted for 39% of two-wheeler loan originations in the first half of 2026, down 19 percentage points from pre-pandemic levels. Meanwhile, 43% of borrowers had more than two years of formal credit history, up from 27% in 2019. Another 18% had less than two years of credit history, indicating that more than 60% of borrowers had an established credit record, according to TU Cibil’s latest report, Shifting Gears 2026: Credit Drives Today’s Mobility.Consumption-led borrowing has contributed to this shift. Nearly a third of two-wheeler borrowers had consumption credit products in their credit histories in the first half of 2026, up from 22% in the corresponding period of 2019. Consumer durable loans featured in the histories of 18% of borrowers, gold loans in 16%, credit cards in 12% and agriculture-related credit products in 8%.Repayment records from small-ticket loans for smartphones, appliances and electronics allow lenders to assess borrowers before extending vehicle finance. The share of borrowers with above-prime CIBIL scores of 801 or higher rose to 16% in June 2026 from 9% in June 2019. The share of prime and above-prime originations increased by 17 percentage points.According to TransUnion CIBIL managing director and CEO Bhavesh Jain, the borrower profile is changing as more consumers enter vehicle finance with established credit histories and subsequently take on other credit products. "Two-wheeler finance is increasingly becoming part of a longer customer journey, with relevance extending well beyond the initial mobility need," he said.Overall vehicle lending grew sharply between June 2019 and June 2026, while delinquencies fell. Two-wheeler loans outstanding rose 3.2 times to Rs 1.76 lakh crore and borrowers 1.9 times to 3.3 crore, while delinquencies fell 128 basis points to 1.4%. Passenger vehicle loans grew 2.6 times to Rs 11 lakh crore, with borrowers rising 1.7 times to 2.5 crore. Average sanctions rose 49% to Rs 8.2 lakh, while delinquencies fell 95 basis points to 0.5%. SUV demand and rising car prices extended average loan tenures by five months to 62 months.Semi-urban and rural markets accounted for 64% of two-wheeler originations and 61% of all vehicle originations in H1 2026, up from 56% in H1 2019. Rural car purchases by two-wheeler upgraders grew 15% annually, against 8% for overall auto loans; these markets accounted for 51% of higher-value car upgrades.NBFCs held 73% of outstanding two-wheeler loans, up 10 percentage points since 2019, against 23% for private banks and 4% for other lenders. They also led passenger vehicle finance with 37%, ahead of public sector banks at 30% and private banks at 26%. Used-car originations were 1.5 times pre-pandemic levels.Two-wheeler loans also opened the door to wider borrowing: 68% of H2 2022 borrowers took another credit product within three years, rising to 84% among those with at least two years of credit history. Within 12-18 months, 41% took consumer durable loans averaging Rs 23,000, 21% personal loans averaging Rs 2.47 lakh, 18% gold loans averaging Rs 1.40 lakh and 14% credit cards averaging Rs 84,000. Another 8% financed passenger vehicles with average sanctions of Rs 8.2 lakh, while 5% took home loans averaging Rs 23.7 lakh.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Medicare scams are showing up in paid search results. Here's what to know.
articles.summary: Here's how you can avoid online Medicare scams this open enrollment season.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

Medicare open enrollment for 2027 begins this week, and the Federal Trade Commission is warning beneficiaries to stay alert to online scams.

Scammers can become more active during open enrollment, when more people are searching for and updating their plan information. This year, the FTC expects many of them to appear in paid search ads. These are sponsored posts that can appear at the top of the search results when you look for Medicare information.

According to the FTC, "Bad actors often use web addresses that look similar to government website addresses. They also use keywords and official-looking logos to make you think you're at the real Healthcare.gov or Medicare.gov when you're not."

Here's what Medicare recipients should look for this open enrollment season , and how to avoid potential scams:

Medicare open enrollment and online fraud

Medicare open enrollment for 2027 runs from Oct. 15 through Dec. 7.

During this window, beneficiaries can review their existing plans, switch from a traditional Medicare plan to a Medicare Advantage plan (or vice versa), change or sign up for a Medicare Part D plan, and more. Beneficiaries typically receive an Annual Notice of Change (ANOC) letter before open enrollment, outlining changes to their plan.

Scams targeting Medicare recipients can happen any time of the year — not just during open enrollment. Common methods scammers use to contact beneficiaries can range from fraudulent phone calls or text messages to fake Medicare representatives at the front door or emails pretending to be from a doctor or insurance company.

Often, they try to get people to pay for a fake plan or service, or they want to access users' Medicare or Social Security numbers to commit identity theft. The National Council on Aging says common tactics include pressuring beneficiaries to switch their Medicare plans, attempting to upgrade or renew their Medicare cards, or threatening to cancel coverage — all with the goal of getting personal information.

With this information, scammers may be able to get medical care, access prescription drugs, or submit claims under your plan, according to the FTC. For the victims of these scams, this could lead to increased costs for medical care they didn't actually receive, and even to inaccurate medical records.

This year, the FTC is specifically warning Medicare beneficiaries about online scams in which bad actors may impersonate government websites. They may imitate government logos and have authentic-looking websites, and then pay to appear at the top of online search results.

But like phone and email scams, clicking those fake ad links could lead beneficiaries to accidentally give away their personal information and expose them to the same identity theft risks.

If you're participating in Medicare open enrollment this year, it's important to take some steps to keep your personal information safe online. Here are some things to keep in mind:

When you're searching for the Medicare website, take time to ensure you choose the right search result. If you just choose the first result you see, you could be directed to the wrong site.

Avoid paid search results, which typically have "ad" or "sponsored" next to them, and scroll down to the non-sponsored results. The official Medicare website will always be a ".gov" site.

When paid-search scammers get you to click on their sponsored results, the websites those links direct you to can look like official government websites. They may even have information about the Medicare plans you're looking for.

However, you should always double-check the web address to make sure you're at the site you meant to navigate to. The official Medicare website is Medicare.gov, and the general health insurance marketplace website is Healthcare.gov. Always look for a ".gov" web address.

You can also avoid search results altogether by typing the correct government URLs into your browser directly.

If you receive an unexpected call from someone claiming to be a Medicare representative, don't give them your Medicare or Social Security number. This is especially true if they're using common scam tactics, such as canceling your coverage or issuing a new Medicare card.

If you're unsure about a call, you can hang up and contact Medicare directly by phone at 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227). Representatives are available 24/7.

If you come across a scam while searching for Medicare information, you can report it to the FTC or on the Medicare.gov website .

articles.title: Battery fires: DGCA bans a make of power bank on all flights to, from and within India
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has barred a particular power bank from being carried on aircraft in either passenger or any
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has barred a particular power bank from being carried on aircraft in either passenger or any cargo flight to, from and within India. The decision comes “In view of the recent fire incident involving the MOBIKINS MK-PB-04 power bank, and considering the potential safety risks associated with it.”“… the travelling public and airlines are hereby advised to ensure that the MOBIKINS MK-PB-04 power bank is not carried or transported on board the aircraft, whether as passenger baggage (including checked-in and cabin baggage) or as cargo, on any flight to, from, or within India. Airlines are further advised to take appropriate measures to identify and prevent the carriage of the aforesaid power bank and to disseminate this safety advisory to the passengers through suitable communication channels,” says a recent order issued by DGCA chief Vir Vikram Yadav.Over the past one year, several countries including India have started restricting power bank usage on aircraft due to the possibility of the same catching fire. Apart from limiting number of power banks and their batter capacity, the same can neither be used to charge a personal electronic devices (PED) nor be charged via the in-seat power source on aircraft.The instance of PED and power bank fires has been on the rise globally. The biggest scare on this front remains airlines taking cabin bags from passengers at boarding gate to be kept in baggage hold of aircraft. These cabin bags may have PEDs, power banks and if a fire breaks out in them in the belly baggage hold, the same won't even get detected easily. The aviation ministry is aware of this issue and is working to resolve it.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Skydance valuation: 'There's no way that this company is worth $111 billion,' media analyst explains
articles.summary: By media analyst Evan Shapiro's reading, the stock market valuing Skydance (SKYD) at $111 billion is "just lazy, and it's incorrect."
articles.body:
By media analyst Evan Shapiro's reading, the stock market valuing Skydance ( SKYD ) at $111 billion is the lazy way of evaluating the newly formed media giant .

The publicly traded shares represent "about 10% of the equity in Skydance, which means that the market is valuing the company at $111 billion," Shapiro told Yahoo Finance Senior Reporter Brooke DiPalma (video above). "That's the price that Ellison paid for Warner Bros. Discovery. That's just lazy, and it's incorrect."

Shapiro's estimate is far lower: His team put Skydance's net asset value at $29 billion, a figure he published in his Media War & Peace newsletter .

Skydance, formed last week when Paramount closed its $111 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, owns the Warner Bros. and Paramount movie studios, the HBO Max and Paramount+ streaming services, and TV networks including CBS, CNN, HBO, TNT, TBS, Nickelodeon, and MTV.

The problem, he said, is that Skydance is "a business whose primary cash flow is coming from fading businesses, linear cable." Shapiro added that the company can't negotiate deals for Warner Bros. and Paramount channels together and must keep the two studios separate.

Then there's the debt: Skydance started out with $81 billion of it, Shapiro said, after taking on $52 billion of new debt to help pay for Warner Bros. Discovery. Billionaire Larry Ellison and Oracle ( ORCL ), the company he co-founded, "are backstopping this company and are expected to provide additional financing should the company get into trouble," Shapiro said.

Oracle has nearly doubled its long-term debt to more than $160 billion over the past two years, Bloomberg recently reported .

"The Ellisons now owe more than the valuation of Disney, Fox, and Roku combined," Shapiro said. By his Skydance figure and Bloomberg's Oracle figure, the two companies owe more than $240 billion, versus the combined value of $236 billion for Disney ( DIS ), Fox ( FOXA ), and Roku ( ROKU ) as of Monday's close.

"So there's no way that this company is worth $111 billion," he said.

What about Wall Street analysts who say the studios' film and TV library alone could justify the price?

Shapiro's answer comes back to debt and why it can't be ignored: "Analysts on Wall Street are actually now articulating the Ellison risk."

The Oracle and Skydance debt "are now intertwined," he said, and the cost of borrowing against it is "substantially higher than it was."

articles.title: Indian Railways exports first 18-coach LHB train for Bangladesh as part of 200 coach order; specially designed coaches feature CCTVs, baby care and prayer rooms, and other passenger-friendly amenities
articles.summary: Indian Railways has exported the first batch of LHB passenger coaches to Bangladesh under a new deal.
articles.body: Indian Railways has exported the first batch of LHB passenger coaches to Bangladesh under a new deal. RITES Ltd announced on Tuesday that it had sent the first batch of 18 broad-gauge passenger coaches to Bangladesh Railway under an agreement to supply a total of 200 coaches.The coaches, which come in seven different variants, are being built at the Rail Coach Factory (RCF) in Kapurthala, Punjab.Dispatched on October 12, 2026, the first rake consists of 11 non-AC Shovan chair cars, three AC chair cars, two AC sleeper coaches and two AC power cars. The power cars are fitted with a guard room and space for luggage, the company said.RITES added that its supplies to date include more than 280 locomotives and over 1,085 coaches and diesel multiple unit (DMU) trainsets.The company, which holds Navratna public sector enterprise status, has executed projects in more than 55 countries across Asia, Africa, Latin America, South America and West Asia.Indian Railways’ coaches for BangladeshAccording to the Ministry of Railways, the partnership between RCF and Bangladesh Railway began in 2015-16, when the Indian factory successfully delivered 120 LHB broad-gauge passenger coaches to the neighbouring country.Also Read | After launching Vande Bharat sleeper train with 16 coaches, Indian Railways now bets on 24-coach variant of new train with pantry car and features better than Rajdhani ExpressBuilding on that collaboration, Bangladesh Railway placed a fresh order through RITES in 2024 for the manufacture and supply of 200 broad-gauge passenger coaches. The order covers seven different variants and further deepens the association between the two organisations.The coaches have been customised to suit Bangladesh Railway's operational requirements while providing passengers with greater comfort.The ministry said the coaches incorporate several design improvements and modifications developed specifically for LHB coaches, including features described as first-of-their-kind.Among these are specially designed reclining seats fitted with stainless steel armrests and footrests. The seating arrangement allows passengers to adjust their seats to different reclining positions.A range of passenger-oriented facilities has also been incorporated. These include fans in air-conditioned coaches, an integrated CCTV surveillance system, a passenger alarm system, windows that can be partially opened, a Baby Care Room and a Prayer Room.The coaches have also been adapted to Bangladesh Railway's operating conditions. Their roofs have been reinforced structurally to bear the additional weight of passengers travelling on top of coaches during periods of heavy passenger traffic.Another important technological feature is a crashworthy design that meets European Standard EN 15227. To achieve the required safety performance, the coach body shell was redesigned to improve its ability to withstand collisions and provide better protection to passengers.The electrical system has also been customised for Bangladesh Railway. Unlike the conventional 750 V system used in coaches operated by Indian Railways, these coaches are designed to function on a 415 V electrical system.Also Read | Delhi-Varanasi in less than 4 hours, Mumbai-Pune in 48 minutes, Chennai-Bengaluru in over 1 hour: Indian Railways bets on seven new bullet train corridors in Rs 16 lakh crore high-speed pushYou use AI every day.
